taste.name: The product is the illustration
taste.trigger: When every section needed a visual to explain a back-office chore (invoicing, receipts, bank sync) to an owner who has never used an ERP
taste.decision: Chose live-looking product fragments filled with believable Spanish business data over abstract illustrations, icons-in-blobs or lifestyle stock photography
taste.reason: Because an owner who fears 'software' trusts what they can recognise: a ticket for 'Café Mar · −4,50 €' booked to 'Dietas' answers 'will this understand my receipts?' faster than any sentence
evidence: Hero visual is an interactive simulation of 14 modules, labelled 'Es una simulación: nada de lo que hagas aquí se guarda'
Mock data: F260014, P260011, 47.320 € saldo, 'Ticket 0042 · 46,54 €', 'Hoy tienes 3 tareas, 1 presupuesto por firmar y 2 leads nuevos'
Photography appears only in the testimonial block; 0 illustration assets elsewhere
Mock UI uses 11-13px text (151 nodes at 13px), deliberately smaller than marketing copy so it reads as 'screen', not 'page'

taste.name: One typeface, hierarchy by tracking and size
taste.trigger: When choosing a type voice for a broad SME audience across 18 sections
taste.decision: Chose a single generic family (Inter, 2,246 nodes) in 400/500/600 with heavy negative tracking at display sizes over a display/body pairing or a characterful brand face
taste.reason: Because the brand wants to sound like a tool, not a magazine: the display weight comes from compression (-2.1px at 56px, line-height 0.98) rather than from a new font the owner would read as 'marketing'
evidence: h1 56px/-2.1px, h2 48px/-1.68px, h3 24px/-0.48px: tracking scales with size
Acknowledged limit: Inter with no modular scale (56/48/24 jump) is a generic choice; the craft is in the tracking, not the face

taste.name: Accent budget: blue only where money is asked for
taste.trigger: When a page with ~15 sections and 4 persistent CTAs risked turning every button into a shout
taste.decision: Chose to spend the saturated blue #1963EF on the primary trial button only and keep every other CTA black/ink or white over painting nav, eyebrows, cards and icons in brand color
taste.reason: Because a visitor scanning a long page learns within one screen that 'blue = start', so the conversion target is findable again at any scroll depth without re-reading
evidence: Blue background area 0% in areaPct; 10 nodes total
Nav CTA #000 pill, sticky bar CTA #121926 pill, dark-band CTA white pill; hero CTA the only blue fill with a blue glow
Brand red appears in two places: the logo and the full stop of the hero h1 ('sitio.')
White 80.3% area, warm stone #FAFAF9 6.2%, dark bands 1%

taste.name: Warm paper, cool ink, hairline cards
taste.trigger: When grouping ~40 feature cards without making the page feel like a dashboard of floating boxes
taste.decision: Chose warm stone surfaces (#FAFAF9, #F5F5F4) edged by a 1px inset hairline #ECEAE6 plus a 4%-opacity ink-tinted shadow over pure-gray cards with visible drop shadows
taste.reason: Because flat warm cards read as paper on a desk: separated but not lifted, so the eye stays on the product fragment inside each card instead of on the card chrome
evidence: Card shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #ECEAE6, 0 1px 2px rgba(18,25,38,0.04): shadow tinted toward text ink #121926, not black
Text ink #121926 is cool navy; surfaces lean warm (stone): deliberate temperature split
Nested radius: 18-20px cards hold 12px tiles and 8px/9999px chips
Two dark #0F1117 bands (scanner, pricing) are the only full-bleed color changes in 17,000px
